title: The cutting contest at Mexico's: Greely Walton, Hawkins, Hodges, Carney and Holmes
summary: At a small 133rd Street joint he heard Greely Walton and Coleman Hawkins, then reluctantly played and was said to have outswung Hodges, which Chick Webb publicized.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: After your initial enthusiasm at the Savoy, and meeting Chick Webb and all these people, did you go back to Boston?
No, not right away. I stayed around. I went to work... I worked... Let me see. I played the next
night at the Savoy. I played for that anniversary thing they was havin'...
Johnny Hodges must have told Chick that you played saxophone.
Oh, well, everybody knew it after I was here the first night, because we went to the cutting contest. That's where I met Greely Walton. Greely was in there blowin' when we come in. And...

On 133rd Street, a little joint down there called Mexico's. Let me see... This little room in here would be about the size of the place -- a little-bitty room. Greely was blowin' when I walked in, which I didn't know Greely, but... Boy, I was amazed. The place was full of musicians, and he's blowin'... Hey, I never heard no saxophone like that. I'm telling you.

And while he's blowin', Hawk walks in, Coleman Hawkins, and he start to blowin'. Well, he was the master, you know. Well, there was something different when he blowed, too. Nobody else would play no more tenor. They wouldn't play it. Couldn't get 'em to play it.
So Johnny taken out his horn. He said, "All right, let's get some of these alto players out here." And he got his horn out, and got to blowin'... Boy, when he got

through, they were applauding for him, and one thing or another. He said, "All right, let some of these other fellows play." "Here, this boy, he can play. Make Harry Carney play." Harry said, "Sure." Sure, he'd play. He'd be glad to play. Taken' his horn out. Got to playing.

So Harry got through and he said, "Make Charlie play. He can play." I said, "Man, what are you talkin' about?" I wasn't thinking about playing. I was scared to death just being in there, you know, with all them sharks and things... They were big men to me. I said, "No, I'm not gonna do no playin'." Well, they begged me to play, so I did play -- what little I knew. And I got to rockin' and carryin' on. So damn, boy, they applauded. Somebody said to Chick Webb, "He's outswinging your man Johnny Hodges!" Boy...
